changelog:
v102: Interactive timeline curation + timeline.md consolidation (viewer evolution phase 4, final). The Timeline was a validation surface you could only read — wrong or missing placements meant a trip to the CLI. Now the unplaced bucket is interactive: each moment gets a period picker + when-hint field + Place button (optionally also filing a --kind date correction so the fact enters the compile layer). Manual placements persist in state/timeline_placements.json (user data, committed by the weekly autocommit), keyed by CONTENT — sha1(source + description)[:12] — so raw sources stay immutable and a reclassification that rewrites a description orphans the placement into a removable stale notice instead of silently misapplying it. place_events gains an optional placements overlay (step 0, backward-compatible default) where the owner's decision outranks every heuristic; placed-by-you moments render a pin badge with an unpin button. wiki/timeline.md is consolidated from a duplicate flat event dump into a thin generated export of timeline.timeline_data() — periods as headers, manual placements honored, explicit Unplaced section — deleting the duplicated event-loading loop and guaranteeing the committed phone-readable page can never contradict the curated view. Tests: test_v102_timeline_curation.py (key stability, save/replace/remove, manual-wins + when-hint override, backward-compat default, unknown-period fallthrough, stale surfacing, place/unplace actions).

v101: Write actions — the viewer becomes a review-and-write studio (viewer evolution phase 3). The browser could see everything and touch nothing; every real action lived in Telegram or the CLI. Now serve_wiki gains a POST surface: a per-process session token (embedded in every form) + localhost Host/Origin checks gate all mutations, every handler shells the existing lifehug.py CLI (never reimplemented), and mutations serialize under a state/.viewer-action.lock mkdir lock so browser POSTs can't race the crons. Review queue: candidates get Promote (mandatory category picker defaulting to the inferred category) / Defer / Dismiss; focus recommendations get Approve (runs as a job — focus_new scaffolds and seeds questions) / Dismiss; the home second-voice card gets a Got-it acknowledge (new question_planner.acknowledge_second_voice_offer + lifehug.py second-voice-ack; acknowledged offers hide from home and still never repeat). Artifact lifecycle on every /artifact-version/ page: direct edit saved as vN+1 (artifact save --model manual-edit), Revise with AI (new artifact revise --feedback subcommand reusing compose's revision prompt + call_ai, extracted save_version helper), mark final, promote-to-source (kicks off a no-AI recompile job), and record delivery with the recipient's reaction. Reflections & corrections: every source row and every Mirror raw signal links to /source-actions — additive reflect-source, fix --wrong/--right, or scoped retraction, plus Recompile-now. New system/jobs.py runs long actions as detached processes (state/jobs/<id>.json + log; the runner finalizes the record so viewer restarts never orphan a job) with a 3s polling pill in the flash banner. Keyless machines never error on AI actions — artifact revision queues an agent task under state/agent_tasks/artifact/. Tests: test_v101_actions.py (auth 403s, redirect+flash, job lifecycle incl. stdin and bad-id guards, second-voice ack, UI surfaces).

v100: The Mirror — introspection gets its first surface (viewer evolution phase 2). 264 contradictions and 494 self-understanding insights (incl. position: entries) sat invisible in state/classifications/. New system/mirror.py distills them into wiki/self/mirror.md, a dated weekly EDITION (never a live profile) under a fixed section contract: Tensions I keep circling / What I seem to know about myself / Stated positions / Sit with (exactly 3 open questions). Voice contract enforced by prompt + validation: second person, 'you've said' never 'you are', tensions as two coexisting truths joined by 'and' (MI developing-discrepancy framing — the author resolves them), every claim cites its sources, no trait verdicts. Weekly maintenance runs mirror-compile after classification; keyless machines emit state/agent_tasks/mirror/ for agent completion via --from-response (the emit no-ops when this week's edition exists — the maintenance skill pre-completes it). /views/mirror renders the edition with the raw signals browsable underneath (tensions/insights/positions, each citing its source); the home page's worth-sitting-with card now draws from the edition's Sit-with picks, falling back to the raw-signal daily pick. lifehug.py gains mirror-compile. Also fixes a latent test-suite landmine: the shared load() helper in 24 test files replaced sys.modules entries with private module copies, splitting monkeypatched state across module objects whenever import order shifted — load() now restores the canonical entry (and the two tests that leaned on the leak bind their own copy).

v99: The viewer home becomes an action hub — invitations lead, the wiki index steps aside. The home page (/) previously dumped wiki/index.md — the least designed surface holding center stage — while the actionable views hid in a flat 15-item hamburger and the two richest introspective datasets (classifier contradictions and self_understanding_insights) rendered nowhere. Now / renders up to five calm invitation cards: a chapter that crossed READY with no draft (book.compute_books), one tension or insight to sit with (deterministic daily pick over state/classifications — the first surface these have ever had; the Mirror synthesis comes next), the week's next unanswered planned question, review counts (open candidates + pending focus recs, counts only), a perennial come due, this month's unacknowledged second-voice offer, and a standing last slot resurfacing one old answer (>=90 days, On This Day style). Tone contract from the 2024-26 reflective-design literature: invitations, never guilt metrics — no streaks, no overdue red, at most one heavy introspective card, absence reads as stillness (a quiet 'the loop is fed' card when nothing waits); a small stats strip below shows state, not debt. Every card loader is failure-wrapped so a broken loader drops its card, never the page. The hamburger menu is regrouped from a flat list into Do (Queue, Candidates, Recommendations, Book) / Reflect (Timeline, Graph; Mirror joins in the next release) / Library (Artifacts, Question Bank, Sources, Privacy) / System (The Loop, Focuses, Coverage, Entities, Reports) — unclaimed views fall into System so adding a view stays one registry entry. The Loop view's counting block is extracted into a shared loop_stats() so home and The Loop can never disagree. CSS gains :root custom properties (palette + primitives for .hub-card/.statstrip) as groundwork for theming. The wiki sidebar is untouched; the index stays one click away. Tests: HomeHubTests in test_wiki_views.py (empty-state calm, full-state card mix, bank-text resolution, second-voice month filter, stable daily pick, menu grouping).

v98: Revisions become visible — version footer, word-level diffs, and a Thoughts group (issue #41). The artifact iteration loop (revise with --feedback until done, v95) had no surface: the Artifacts view rendered only the latest vN.md, so revisions were invisible and incomparable. Now every piece ends with a revision footer — one numbered link per saved version, ★ on the final, hover tooltip carrying that version's created date, model, and --feedback note, plus a Δ link per revision. Two new traversal-guarded routes (modeled on /artifact-file/): /artifact-version/<slug>/<n> renders one revision with prev/next/compare nav and its revision note; /artifact-diff/<slug>/<a>/<b> renders a word-level diff (difflib.SequenceMatcher over word tokens with paragraph breaks preserved) as green <ins> / red <del> spans with add/remove counts. Both are factored into testable helpers (artifact_version_html/artifact_diff_html) with thin do_GET branches; guards reject absolute paths, '..', multi-segment slugs, non-numeric versions, and unknown targets. Also: essays with no Focus now group under a THOUGHTS bar — the author's stated positions — instead of the Unfiled repair-hint group (an opinion essay isn't a metadata orphan); Unfiled keeps its role for genuine orphans. Tests in tests/test_wiki_views.py (RevisionFooterTests).

v97: Theme graduation parity — the theme roster (issues #39/#40). Themes were the only entity type without a roster: pages could only graduate from the frozen 8-key THEME_KEYWORDS dict, while the classifier's 43-item taxonomy and recommend_focuses' theme candidates died at the wiki boundary — 'parenting' could never get a page no matter how much material was about it. Now: (1) entity_roster gains --type theme (thresholds 6.0/2; qualify rule: a recurring theme the story keeps returning to, merging synonyms and abstraction levels); candidates come free from recommendation state; each entry carries AI-curated `keywords` — the surface phrases the compiler matches sources with, the dynamic replacement for a static THEME_KEYWORDS row; normalize prepends the theme's own name, apply_previous_decisions carries curated keywords forward when a refresh response drops them, and the deterministic keyless fallback only accepts names vouched for by the classifier taxonomy or an existing theme page (v90 lesson: junk never stateless-refreshes in). (2) plan_themes reads theme_keyword_map: the static dict overlaid by page-eligible roster themes — roster wins on collision, static remains the fresh-install bootstrap, the 8 legacy pages keep their slugs and origin focus; roster-added themes are origin mention, theme joins _MENTION_CLEANUP_TYPES, so a theme that leaves the roster loses its page via the existing guard-railed orphan cleanup. No roster → byte-identical behavior (regression-pinned). (3) Every theme page seed_relates to the author hub (author_full slug threaded into plan_themes), so themes are reachable from Self with reciprocal backlinks. (4) THEME_TAXONOMY += parenting, marriage, aging, and the classifier may name a genuinely-missing central theme — the roster curates what leaks through (open-vocabulary extraction was rejected: it fragments what the roster would just re-merge). (5) Loop wiring: monthly_research loops theme in both roster passes (keyed + keyless emit-task), skills/maintenance documents the keywords ask, doctor watches theme roster continuity, lifehug.py entity-roster accepts the type. With v95/v96 this completes the opinion lane: opinion → seeded essay → promote → classify → theme roster → wiki/themes/<domain>.md citing the opinion as primary and the essay as supporting. Tests in tests/test_v97_theme_roster.py.

v96: Opinion lane phase 2 — the classifier understands stated positions (issue #39). Opinion sources reached the weekly classifier as if they were event narratives: scene-slot probes and event extraction made no sense for a philosophical position, and the positions themselves were never distilled anywhere. Now build_prompt appends an OPINION ADDENDUM strictly when the source's type is opinion (every other source's prompt is byte-identical — pinned by a prefix-equality regression test): treat the source as a stated position, not an event account; distill each distinct position into self_understanding_insights prefixed 'position: ' (reusing the existing field — zero schema change — so research_expand.load_classified_self_signals grounds the monthly self-arc in the author's actual positions automatically); contradictions only for genuine tensions within or between positions; events usually empty; candidate questions use the Socratic families (origin→value, lived counterexample→contradiction, evolution→growth_edge, dissent→perception_by_others, cost/protection→fear) plus one Gornick grounding question asking for a lived moment behind the belief. Keyless --emit-prompts/--from-response inherit the addendum with no changes. Also: TYPE_TO_WIKI_DIR gains 'self' → wiki/self (latent v15 gap — a self-type Focus never got its wiki node link), and a cross-module contract test pins opinion-candidate story_functions to the planner's SELF_FUNCTIONS vocabulary so the weekly self-knowledge floor keeps selecting them. Tests in tests/test_v96_opinion_loop.py.

v95: Opinion lane phase 1 — capture a stated position, develop it as a seeded essay. An opinion (a philosophical position, a lens on life) had no home: ingest reframed it into narrative scene prompts, no essay format existed, and artifacts couldn't be written FROM a fresh statement (the never-invent rule required everything to pre-exist in the archive). Now: (1) `ingest-story --kind opinion` stores it as an immutable `type: opinion` primary source and generates SOCRATIC follow-up candidates instead of scene prompts — origin, counterexample, evolution, dissent, stakes — each carrying a planner SELF_FUNCTIONS story_function so the weekly self-knowledge slot draws from them with zero planner changes; rejected with --witness; prints the composed next step. (2) New `essay` artifact format + templates/essay.md: the thesis is the author's stated position, argument and generalization allowed, grounded in life material where the pack offers it, steelman welcome, 600-1500 words. (3) `artifact new --seed <source-path>` injects that source verbatim as the FIRST context-pack section (un-truncated to 8k chars — the seed IS the thesis, never a snippet), records seed_source in artifact.json, and appends a SEED DEVELOPMENT block to the prompt: the seed needs no corroboration; never-invent still binds biographical events/quotes/other people but not reasoning that develops the position. Seeded-and-unscoped packs skip the Source Answers dump (the empty-categories whole-corpus path) and fall back to the seed's title for wiki/prior-artifact matching; explicit --categories/--subject behave exactly as before, and non-seeded calls are byte-identical. The iteration contract is documented end-to-end (CLAUDE.md Opinions & Essays, artifact skill, AGENTS.md, READMEs): revise with `artifact save --feedback` until the author says done; done = final + promote-source + compile, turning the essay into source material that influences the wiki (theme pages, the author hub) — artifacts never directly create pages. Phone trigger: messages starting `opinion:`. Gornick rationale in research.md §7b: an opinion is story without situation; the essay and the Socratic loop supply the situation. Tests in tests/test_v95_opinion_essay.py.

v94: Artifacts view groups are collapsible bars (refines #37). Each Focus group renders as a collapsed full-width bar — the Question Bank / Timeline idiom — showing the piece count, focus type, deliverable, and categories on the bar itself, so the full suite of Focuses is scannable at a glance; click a bar to expand into its pieces.

v93: classify_stem is capped under the 255-byte filename limit. A retraction slug embeds the full question text; one real 262-char stem made classification_path unwritable on the keyed path and crashed --emit-prompts on the keyless path. Stems over 180 chars are truncated and made unique with a stable 12-char sha256 suffix; stems at or under the cap stay byte-identical, so existing classification files keep matching. Found while verifying v92 on live data.

v92: keyless agent mode reaches the maintenance Loop (closes #38). Every AI module already had a keyless agent path (classify_story --prompt/--from-response, entity_roster --emit-task/--from-response, research_expand --prompt/--from-response, compile --emit-tasks) but the weekly/monthly orchestrators never routed to them — on a machine with no gateway and no key they just recorded raw learning failures. Now: (1) `lifehug.py ai-status` reports the AI route (gateway/sdk-key) and exits 1 when keyless; (2) classify_story gains `--classify-all --emit-prompts DIR` — one prompt per pending source plus a manifest.json, mirroring entity_roster --emit-task; the lifehug.py wrapper passes through --emit-prompts/--from-response/--source; (3) weekly_maintenance.sh, when keyless, emits classification tasks to state/agent_tasks/classify (⏸ tasks, not failures) — keyed behavior unchanged; (4) monthly_research.sh, when keyless, emits roster tasks (state/agent_tasks/roster/<type>.json) and research-expansion prompts (state/agent_tasks/research/) instead of failing; it never falls back to the deterministic roster (v90 lesson); (5) new skills/maintenance/SKILL.md — the desktop protocol: check ai-status, pre-complete AI work as the model (classify first, so the week's queue sees the week's answers), run the script, or complete tasks a keyless cron left behind. state/agent_tasks/ is transient and gitignored.

v91: Artifacts view grouped by Focus (closes #37). The flat slug list is gone: pieces group under the person/project they belong to (category -> focus from the roadmap, subject fallback), person groups append the subject's real name ("Mom (Desi)"), occasions like Mother's Day are badges rather than groups, titles are humanized, and metadata orphans land in an Unfiled group with a repair hint. PDF/image sidecars are linked and served via a new traversal-guarded /artifact-file/ route. artifact new/save now record occasion in meta.yaml. Fixed the dead 'promoted to source' badge, which read a never-written artifact.json key (promotions) instead of promoted_sources.

v90: AJ becomes a person (closes #36). Three compounding defects kept a heavily-mentioned person out of the wiki: (1) _build_entity_stats read question_id/answer_id but classification files carry only source_path, so every classification-derived entity had zero unique_answers and could never clear the roster gate — qid now derives from source_path via answer_id_from_filename; (2) an operator-precedence bug (`x.get('name') or x if isinstance(x, str) else None`) silently skipped dict entries and CRASHED the whole recommend-focuses run on string entries (hidden by `|| true` in monthly_research.sh since the v79 backfill) — entries of both shapes now record; (3) role-word lock-in: v67's settled-decisions fold renamed a resolved proper name (AJ) back to its role-word canonical (Brother) forever — a bare role-word canonical now yields to a proper name, demoting to an alias, with the matching exception added to the resolver prompt. The v66 two-letter thresholds were never the regression and remain live. Regression tests: tests/test_v90_aj_regression.py.

v89: answer_body no longer swallows an answer behind its follow-up divider. The extractor treated the `---` before a generated '## Follow-up Questions Generated' section as a body wrapper and returned everything AFTER it — so any answer with that layout (2 of 121 on the live instance, including N10's Iron Man moment) compiled as just its follow-up list. When the captured segment is the follow-up section, the answer text preceding the divider is returned instead; all other answers' bodies are byte-identical (no synthesis-cache churn). Found while verifying v88.

v88: Retractions bind to content, not to an id forever (the N10/Iron-Man case). A retraction filed against mis-filed content kept suppressing the id after the genuine answer replaced it — Dave's real N10 answer (Charlee compared him to Iron Man) vanished from the wiki because an earlier retraction of the mis-filed Father's Day letter targeted answer:N10 globally. Within the v74 design: (1) new retractions pin the target's payload sha (retracts_sha256) at filing time, and compile-time resolution skips a pinned retraction whose target content has since changed — retract the CONTENT, not the id; (2) `lifehug.py unretract <retraction> --reason` voids a wrong retraction explicitly (adds voided/voided_at/voided_reason directive metadata; the record and its original reason stay for the audit trail); legacy unpinned retractions keep applying unchanged. Also fixes why Charlee's page showed 'no source material' despite her Father's Day letter existing: (3) witness accounts attach to their person's page by witness_slug matched against every known page name — a letter FROM Charlee is source material for Charlee's page even if it never says her name; (4) a brand-new Focus derives a first-name alias from its title ('Charlee Joy Taylor' → 'Charlee') so mention enrichment works before the monthly roster refresh knows the person; (5) the page banner no longer claims answered prompts the retraction filter then drops (counts computed after filtering). Tests in tests/test_v88_retraction_repair.py.

v87: Summary failure lines pick the informative line. A recorded learning failure often contains the step's entire captured output (retry noise included); the weekly summary squashed it into gibberish like 'timed out Error: timed out Error: timed out…'. _failure_label now selects the first Error-marked line (else the first non-empty line) before condensing, so the message reads 'C16 — timed out'. Found during v86's live verification against real state.

v86: Scannable maintenance reports (closes issue #35). The weekly/monthly Telegram message was the raw concatenated stdout of every step — an unreadable wall of text on a phone. Now Telegram carries a short counts-first summary and the full report becomes a document. New system/weekly_report.py (`lifehug.py weekly-summary --since <iso>`) derives the summary from STATE FILES, never by parsing step output: classification successes (state/classifications timestamps) and failures (learning_failures.jsonl) as `N ✅ M ❌` with one-line per-file reasons; candidates new/promoted/backlog; queue size + expiry; coverage answered/total + GREEN count; non-classify failures; pending Focus recommendations; doctor verdict (piped from the cron run so checks don't execute twice — standalone runs execute them in-process). Sections render only when non-empty; every line is phone-width; the whole message fits one Telegram chunk. The full step-by-step output is persisted to state/reports/weekly-YYYY-MM-DD.md (and monthly-*.md) BEFORE safe_autocommit, so it's committed and readable from the phone via GitHub; the wiki viewer gains a Reports view (/views/reports) rendering them newest-first. The second-voice offer and present-tense capture prompt stay in the Telegram message (they're asks, not logs). monthly_research.sh gets the identical treatment via `weekly-summary --kind monthly`. Dry runs preview the summary. Tests in tests/test_v86_weekly_report.py pin the section formats, the one-chunk size cap, and the orchestrator contract (no raw ${*_OUT} interpolation into telegram_notify).

v85: Resilient AI routing — ship the gateway fixes properly (issue #34 workaround). Folds in the unreleased 2026-07-05 hotfixes (AI timeout 120s→600s with ai_timeout_seconds config / LIFEHUG_AI_TIMEOUT env overrides; gateway retry logic) and fixes what the audit found in them. (1) The claimed gateway→retry→SDK fall-through now actually exists: call_ai previously RAISED after exhausting gateway retries and only used the Anthropic SDK when no gateway was configured at all — so on any machine running OpenClaw, the deterministic 'Agent couldn't generate a response' rejection (the gateway's quality checker refuses JSON-only output; lifehug/lifehug#34) burned three full generations plus 20s of sleeps and then failed anyway. Now: transient gateway failures (5xx, timeouts, connection errors) retry up to 3x then fall through to the SDK; the deterministic sentinel is never retried and falls through immediately; without an API key the original gateway error is re-raised (not the missing-key complaint). (2) The classifier DEFAULT_MODEL downgrade to claude-sonnet-4-6 is reverted to claude-sonnet-5 — the 'deprecated/404' diagnosis contradicts Anthropic's current model catalog (claude-sonnet-5 is the active current Sonnet; sonnet-4-6 is previous-generation) and could not be reproduced; if the 404 recurs on an instance, set classify_model in config.yaml and capture the real error. Tests in tests/test_v85_ai_routing.py pin the routing matrix and the model default. The real fix for #34 (the gateway accepting JSON-only completions) belongs in OpenClaw.

v84: Updater preserves executable bits. Path.write_bytes creates NEW files as 0o644, so an executable framework script arriving via update landed without its exec bit (seen live: file_answer_bg.sh applied as rw-r--r-- while long-existing .sh files kept 755 only because writes to existing files preserve mode). Third updater file-corruption bug of the v56 class (trailing-newline loss, protection shadowing, now mode loss). apply_version now reads each file's git mode from the tag (ls-tree) and chmods +x when the tag says 100755 — and because every apply rewrites all framework files, instances with an already-stripped copy get repaired on their next update. Test in tests/test_update.py.

v83: Detached answer filer hardened (audit of v82). The fire-and-forget contract is unchanged — chat dispatches file_answer_bg.sh with nohup + &, acks immediately, exits its turn, and the script sends its own confirmation when filing completes. What changed is the reliability of that confirmation leg, which the audit found could silently vanish: the script reimplemented Telegram sending with a strictly weaker copy of the framework's plumbing (token only from ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json — no TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN env; chat id only from telegram_chat_id — no group_chat_id fallback; PyYAML required; no 4096-char chunking, so a failure message carrying a traceback would be rejected by Telegram and swallowed). Notification now goes through `lifehug.py notify` (send_telegram: env-first token, group fallback, yaml-free config parsing, chunked, always exits 0 so it can never fail the filing). Concurrent filings serialize on a portable mkdir lock (state/.filing.lock) with a 15-min stale-steal and a ~4-min wait ceiling — after which the filing proceeds anyway (a rare race beats a dropped answer) and says so in the confirmation. The framework-standard TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID env override is honored; LIFEHUG_CHAT_ID is kept as a back-compat alias. The chat/phone detached-filing flow is now documented in CLAUDE.md's Processing an Answer section, putting the wrapper In the Loop. Tests in tests/test_v83_filer.py.

v82: Two chat-critical fixes.

(1) Self-contained follow-up questions. Adaptive follow-ups can fire as standalone daily prompts months after the parent question was asked — but the follow-up generator prompt allowed bare pronouns ('her', 'him', 'them') whose antecedent lived only in the parent question or the author's previous answer, so the question read as broken when it fired alone. Example: C16 'You said you wish you could talk to her now...' with no referent for 'her'. Added SELF-CONTAINED RULE #0 at the top of gen_followups.py design principles: name every person/place/thing, never use bare pronouns whose antecedent lives outside the question itself, verify by reading the draft as if you'd never seen the parent question. This is the highest-priority rule because it's the difference between a usable standalone question and a broken one.

(2) Detached answer filer. process_answer inline-runs wiki_compile which calls an LLM per synthesized page (30-90s), which exceeds chat model idle timeouts and kills the confirmation reply even though the answer filed correctly. New system/file_answer_bg.sh — chat dispatches with nohup + &, chat exits its turn immediately, the script runs process-answer to completion and sends its own Telegram confirmation ('✅ Filed X · Coverage: N/M') via the bot token. Chat destination is env-override LIFEHUG_CHAT_ID or read from profile.yaml/config.yaml telegram_chat_id, so the wrapper works for any Lifehug instance. Add the wrapper to the group's systemPrompt as the standard filing flow to adopt.

v81: Timeline rows are real click targets. Feedback on v80: the collapsed periods were hard to click — the summary was a bare text line, and the big brown spine dot (a pseudo-element of the non-interactive details) did nothing when clicked. Period summaries now render as full-width padded rows in the question-bank v61 style (flex layout, background, hover state, leading caret), the spine dot moved onto the summary itself so clicking the dot also toggles, and the counts sit right-aligned in the row. The Unplaced bucket is now collapsible the same way — a summary row with its own counts (moments · connections) — and expand all / collapse all reaches it too.

v80: Collapsible timeline periods. The /views/timeline spine was fully expanded — every period's entity chips, event dots, and gap cards rendered inline, so the whole timeline was long and hard to scan. Each period is now a native <details> element, collapsed by default: the folded row shows the period name (still a link to its page), chapter bands, and a counts line (N source(s) · N connection(s) · N moment(s) · ◌ N gap(s), plus the no-chronological-order note) so the compact view stays informative; clicking a period expands its chips, moments, overflow, and gap cards. An 'expand all · collapse all' control sits above the spine. Zero-JS core (browser disclosure widget with a rotating caret, matching the question-bank v61 idiom); the unplaced bucket, global gaps, and footer are unchanged. Tests in tests/test_v79_timeline.py.

v79: Visual Timeline — the life graph projected onto time (issue #33). New /views/timeline: a vertical spine of chrono-ordered period entities; every other entity (people, places, objects, projects) lined up against them by SOURCE OVERLAP — an entity's dot sits in the period whose sources overlap its own the most, with the shared source ids rendered as evidence (provable placement, no keyword fuzz; multi-period entities get 'also appears in' chips; zero overlap lands in an explicit unplaced bucket, never forced). Classifier events render as dated dots (author's own time-words + landmark anchors) or visually-distinct undated dots, placed by source membership with era-keyword fallback. The owner's Life Chapters (chapters-exercise source) run as a parallel band of his own era names, aligned best-effort — misalignment is itself feedback. Gaps are first-class: amber cards for eventless periods, all-undated periods, thin lineups, unplaced items, each with a fill-it hint; the footer states the feedback contract (fix/retraction or just tell the bot). New system/timeline.py assembles the data read-only with zero AI calls. classify_story.py gains the keyless path (--from-response --source, mirroring entity_roster/research_expand) plus --no-candidates for archive backfills where hundreds of generated candidates would flood the review store. Tests in tests/test_v79_timeline.py.

v78: Artifacts view in the wiki viewer. outputs/ pieces (letters, posts, captions, chapter drafts) were invisible in the browser — only the Book view's word counts and the compose.py CLI listed them. /views/artifacts now shows every artifact with format, subject, versions, word count, delivered/promoted badges, and the latest version's full text readable inline (collapsible), since outputs/ lives outside the wiki page tree.

v77: Book Assembly audit fix — scene-slot contract. An audit of the v75/v76 book surface found book.FIVE_SLOTS used invented slot names (when_where, meaning_for_self) instead of the classifier's actual scene_slots schema (when_and_where, what_it_says_about_me) — two of five slots would silently never match, capping every chapter's scene depth at 60% once real classifications landed. Names aligned; a cross-module contract test now pins book.FIVE_SLOTS against the classify_story prompt schema so this class of drift fails loudly; unused ANSWERS_DIR constant removed. Everything else in the audit passed: meta.yaml parsing matches compose's writer, offer state machine correct (send-failure retries, drafted chapters never re-offer, dry-run never marks), planner boost capped and eligibility-gated, milestone hook failure-wrapped.

v76: Book assembly phase 2 — the book actively drives itself (issue #30). Phase 1 showed the manuscript shape; phase 2 makes the system push. (1) Milestone chapter-ready offers: when an answer tips a chapter into READY, process_answer fires a one-time Telegram nudge with the exact `lifehug.py artifact new --format chapter` command inline; state/book_offers.json tracks fired offers so a chapter is announced exactly once per crossing, chapters that already have a draft never re-offer, and the send is best-effort (silent no-op on missing credentials, learning_failures.jsonl on error, capture never blocks). New `lifehug.py book-offers [--send]` gives operator preview/manual-fire. (2) Manuscript rollup: `book.py` scans `outputs/` for chapter-format drafts, matches them to categories via each artifact's meta.yaml (a draft that weaves Origins+Becoming counts toward both), takes only the LATEST vN.md so revisions replace not sum, and reports `drafted_words` + `manuscript_target` (categories × 350) + ratio per chapter and per book. Header line + wiki table gain a Draft column showing words/percent; chapters with drafts show a 📄 badge. (3) Chapter-gap boost in the planner: `book.gap_question_ids()` surfaces top-priority unanswered questions from chapters at NEARLY_READY_MIN≤sat<READY (0.50– 0.70), ranked by proximity-to-READY first. `question_planner.build_queue` reserves ~15% of the week (new `chapter_boost_fraction` in DEFAULT_LANE_POLICY) for these boosted picks BEFORE the general weighted sampling, capped so it can't crowd out the rest of the Focus mix. Allocation metadata now carries a `chapter_boost` block with cap/taken. Silent no-op when the book module can't import. (4) Compose-don't-summarize hardened in templates/chapter.md: explicit hard-rules block forbidding Q&A transcripts, bullet lists, table-of-contents structure, fact/dialogue/people the source didn't provide, psychology explanations, and moral wrap-ups; a positive spec for what compose IS — the author's exact words lightly stitched, scenes not summaries, chronology serving story. Fixes the outputs/my-katie failure mode where an artifact came out as a Q&A transcript instead of a composed piece. Tests in tests/test_v75_book.py (16 total, +7 for phase 2). Closes phase 2 of lifehug/lifehug#30; phase 3 (word-count-based chapter completion offers, retell-count provenance) still deferred.

v75: Book assembly phase 1 (issue #30). The flagship deliverable was an abstract goal with no path to existence — 109 answers in, the system had never surfaced a chapter or offered one to draft. Book Assembly turns the roadmap into a manuscript view: every Focus whose deliverable is book/chapter/memoir/manuscript becomes a book, and each of its question categories becomes a chapter. Per chapter: answered ratio + progress bar, scene-slot depth from the v70/v71 classifier's five-slot data (McAdams' scene probe), a readiness verdict (EARLY/DEVELOPING/READY/SATURATED) sharing the same threshold vocabulary as progress.py, a manuscript hook linking to the wiki life-arc page that already synthesizes the material, top 5 priority-ranked gap questions to record next, and — when READY — the artifact draft command inline. New system/book.py (compute_books/compute_chapter, no AI calls), lifehug.py subcommands `book-status` (overview) and `book-chapter <book> <chapter>` (depth view with next questions), and a Book Assembly wiki view at /views/book (registered right after The Loop + Graph in the hamburger menu, wide layout, VIEW_DESCRIPTIONS entry). Primary Focus sorts first; zombie focuses (no categories) are skipped. Every readiness number degrades honestly on missing classifications (unclassified answers count as 0/5 slot depth, never faked as full). Tests in tests/test_v75_book.py. Deferred to phase 2: milestone chapter-ready offers to Telegram, word-count-toward-manuscript progress once drafts land in outputs/, book-level gap questions promoted to the weekly queue, and the retell/composition guard (compose-don't-summarize enforced across artifact paths). Closes phase 1 of lifehug/lifehug#30.

v74: Corrections that actually correct (issue #24). Corrections were a write-only dead end — you could file one, but wiki_compile never read it, so the false fact re-appeared on every compile. Now a resolution pass runs before planning: correction sources attach to their targets under an authoritative marker ([LATER CORRECTION — authoritative]) that every downstream consumer sees (synthesis prompts get an explicit override instruction; the changed body re-keys the synthesis cache so affected pages re-render), and new RETRACTION records (source_integrity retract / lifehug.py retract-source) tell the compiler to stop asserting a source — globally, or scoped to specific page slugs via suppress_on for the mis-attribution case (a source that belongs on one person's pages but was wrongly pulled onto another's; the live example: answers/L20.md is about Katie and was cited on the author's childhood page). Raw files stay immutable throughout; corrections/retractions are additive records in sources/corrections/ and lint validates their targets. The classifier prompt now includes a source's corrections so corrected-away facts are never re-derived into entities or candidates. One-line phone-friendly entrypoint: `lifehug.py fix <target> --wrong ... --right ...` files a correction; `--retract [--from-page slug]` files a retraction. Tests in tests/test_v74_corrections.py. Closes lifehug/lifehug#24.

v73: Privacy phase 0 — the synthesis unlock. The owner asked for one thing now: speak freely to the system without fearing exposure, and stop the synthesis from sanitizing. The contract (system/privacy_design.md): raw sources NEVER leave; the compiled wiki is the owner tier — permanently private and fully honest; audience surfaces (public/friends/family) will be SEPARATE owner-reviewed builds generated later — filter at build time, never at read time; everything unlabeled defaults to private, so tiers only ever open material through explicit review, never expose it. Shipped: (1) the synthesis prompt (and keyless task payload) now carries the owner-only honesty contract — do not sanitize difficult material; CACHE_VERSION bumped to v3 so every page re-synthesizes unsanitized (this restores the marriage-repair truth to the Dave & Katie page); (2) sensitivity vocabulary (public < friends < family < private) with rank/floor/visibility helpers in lifehug_core; optional --sensitivity on process-answer and ingest-story (default private); the weekly classifier suggests suggested_sensitivity + reason per source using the recorded taxonomy (children's material hard-capped at family); wiki pages carry a computed sensitivity floor (most-closed cited source, legacy 'personal' reads as private); (3) the local viewer gains a Privacy Preview view (/views/privacy) showing what each future build would be eligible to include — explicitly a preview, never a security boundary. Deferred by design: graduated export builds land with the book work (#30), real auth lands at deployment (#10). Tests in tests/test_v73_privacy.py.

v72: Second voice (Tiers 1-3) — witness accounts, capped offers, interview packs, unsent & legacy letters. Owner-decided cadence model: burden-first, pull not push. Tier 1 (the backbone, zero schedule): `ingest-story --witness <person>` saves ANOTHER PERSON's words as a witness_account source — attributed by name, never merged with the author's account; the synthesis prompt marks witness material explicitly and preserves conflicting tellings side by side ('perspectives differ' is data about the relationship, never an error to resolve); witness ingest generates gap-focused follow-ups for the author (where do the tellings differ, what did they see that you missed). Tier 2 (offers, never tasks): at most second_voice_offers_per_month (default 2, 0 disables) single-line suggestions in the weekly summary — 'if it comes up naturally, ask Mom …' — with offered questions tracked so an ignored offer expires silently and never repeats. Tier 3 (on demand only): `interview-pack <person> --relationship <type>` prints a StoryCorps-style question pack (parent, grandparent, spouse, child, sibling, mentor, cofounder, friend, remembering), personalized with the person's wiki-page gaps, ending with the witness-ingest command. Tier 4 (the bot messaging guests directly) is deliberately deferred to #32 pending multi-recipient infrastructure. New artifact formats: unsent_letter (therapeutic, owner-only, never suggested for sharing; 'hello again' framing for the deceased) and legacy_letter (ethical-will: values → lessons → gratitude → hopes/blessings → forgiveness, built from the author's real material). `artifact delivered` records that a piece was actually given (--to, --note) and can ingest the recipient's reaction as their witness account — a letter isn't done until it's given. Planner: Aron escalation gate (late-arc relational questions — tension, how-they-see-me, what-I-want-them-to-know — held until the person's category has ≥2 answers), Gottman love-map staleness boost (living-person categories quiet ≥60 days get 1.3x), and completed relational arcs earn the Final-Card letter offer + closing reflection in progress. Tests in tests/test_v72_second_voice.py. Closes lifehug/lifehug#29.

v71: Time & self — chapters, perennials, resurfacing, present tense, and a synthesis that talks back. Time-period neighborhoods now follow a six-step chapter arc (PERIOD_ARC: name & bound the chapter → life structure and the Dream → typical day with era anchors → key scenes via the five slots → the transition out including the inner ending and Bridges' neutral zone → the later evaluative look back), with a LIFE-CHAPTER MODE prompt and a hard dating rule: never ask 'what year' — landmark anchors only. The classifier extracts datable `events` (author's own time words + nearest landmark, never inferred years) and compile builds wiki/timeline.md from them. Perennial questions (`lifehug.py perennial-add`, 10Q model) re-ask yearly WITH last year's answer attached — the monthly cron generates due re-asks; `chapters-exercise` prints the annual McAdams table-of-contents ritual. The monthly cron also resurfaces one old answer (≥90 days) verbatim with a reflection question (Echo, CHI 2013 — the one mechanism here with direct experimental well-being evidence), and the weekly summary ends with a rotating present-tense capture prompt so the archive learns this year, not just childhood. The synthesis→question loop closes: non-boilerplate Open Questions from compiled wiki pages harvest into the candidate store (capped 3/week, near-dup guarded) — before this, compile was a dead end for question generation. Deferred to a follow-up issue: full event-history-calendar onboarding survey, values ledger with importance–consistency gaps, Johari coverage metric, retell-count provenance flags. Closes lifehug/lifehug#28.

v70: Question craft v2 — the interviewer gets an education. Every question-generation surface (classifier, follow-up generator, research expansion, artifact prompts) now carries verified interviewing methodology: the two-sentence rule (one sentence of context quoting the author, then ONE open question); McAdams' five-slot scene probe (the classifier extracts scene_slots per source and follow-ups target the empty slots — 'what does it say about you?' being the highest-value ask); the action↔identity ladder; Gornick situation-vs-story tagging; and the high-yield question families (typical-day reconstruction, era anchors, photo/song cues, perspective-taking, off-script probes, forgiveness/blessing). Introspection guardrails: a why→what lint in check_quality parks self-directed why-questions (they confabulate and brood); a rumination detector (LIWC-lite insight/negative/I-rate signals now captured per answer) cools categories showing the brooding signature by 4x in the planner — depth ≠ repetition; and a fresh-upheaval deferral lets the classifier flag deep-processing questions on recent upheavals to wait 60 days (Pennebaker boundary condition), exempt from expiry while waiting. Anti-fossilization: depth passes must ask for never-told angles, follow-ups never restate the author's account, and artifact prompts gain hard voice-preservation rules (your words lightly stitched, never rewritten; compose, don't summarize). Birren's under-covered GAB themes (health/body, death/mortality) joined gap detection so the monthly research proposes them. system/research.md v2 is the central methodology guide with per-item implementation status. Tests in tests/test_v70_v71_craft.py. Closes lifehug/lifehug#27.

v69: Stop the signal bleed — one story-function vocabulary, every classifier field consumed, real feedback attribution. The learning loop leaked most of its signal at internal seams: the quality profile ran its own story-function guesser emitting names (origin_story, stakes_and_risk) that existed nowhere else, so its strongest finding multiplied nothing; half the weekly classifier's output (focus_opportunities, contradictions, self_understanding_insights, possible_outputs) was write-only; by_focus quality attribution was 100% unknown (process_answer hardcoded focus=None); Focus-recommendation approval was a no-op that printed 'manual step'; and planner group/source_type caps were decorative. Fixed: (1) the profile classifies through the planner's shared keyword classifier and normalizes legacy score names on aggregation, so pre-v69 scores keep contributing; (2) focus_opportunities now feed recommend_focuses with evidence-strength boosts; contradictions + self_understanding_insights ground the monthly self-arc prompt in the author's OBSERVED patterns; possible_outputs surface as artifact ideas in progress; (3) answers attribute their owning Focus via the roadmap (both live and retroactive scoring), and the dead wiki_nodes_added file-count signal is retired at weight 0 with weights renormalized; quality scoring no longer silently skips under --no-compile-wiki; (4) recommendation approval actually creates the Focus (roadmap.focus_new: category + registration + starter questions — never a zombie), recommendations dedupe against existing wiki pages (Money/Family/Belonging duplicated live theme pages), and pending recommendations surface in the weekly Telegram summary with the approve command; (5) group caps are now enforced in build_queue like story-function caps, meaningless source_type caps removed, and monthly research consumes the planner's expansion urgency (below 0.25 → no new gap neighborhoods that month; the archive deepens instead of widening); (6) hygiene — user names removed from framework keyword lists, dated model snapshots replaced with current non-dated aliases (claude-sonnet-5 / claude-opus-4-8), dead placeholder removed. Zombie Focuses are excluded from progress totals and listed explicitly. Tests in tests/test_v69_signal.py.

v68: The Loop actually loops — candidate economics, health checks, loud failures, adaptive cadence. An audit found the learning half of the Loop had never completed a cycle: 0 of 56 candidates ever promoted, a weekly cap (2/week) that could never drain ~20/month of inflow, needs_review as a one-way graveyard, 4 zombie Focuses with no question categories silently suppressing research expansion, git-push failures aborting the daily question before delivery, and >4096-char Telegram summaries vanishing silently. Fixed: (1) candidate economics — the weekly cap now scales with backlog pressure (up to 8), semantic near-duplicate detection (token Jaccard) parks reworded dupes, stale candidates expire after 45 days (deferred exempt), score/quality-parked needs_review candidates are re-scored every run so they can graduate as the quality profile shifts, and the research.md craft heuristics (check_quality) now gate promotion instead of being display-only; (2) zombie Focuses are excluded from global_fullness and flagged in planner-report and doctor; (3) doctor gains Loop-rot checks (queue expiry/exhaustion, candidate backlog age, weekly/monthly cadence stalls, empty rosters, zombie Focuses, classification coverage) and runs at the end of every weekly maintenance with warnings in the Telegram summary; (4) failures are loud — monthly research records learning failures (roster refreshes individually wrapped), weekly quality-update/auto-promote/planner-queue are wrapped, all three flows use the new chunked `lifehug.py notify` (summaries split under Telegram's 4096-char cap), and git housekeeping pulls-rebases before pushing and can no longer abort question delivery (daily sends the question FIRST); (5) adaptive cadence 1-3/day — after an answer is processed, an optional same-day follow-up question is offered (config max_questions_per_day, default 3, never after 20:00), after 4+ silent days the daily pick switches to a short, warm re-engagement question instead of re-offering the heavy queue head (config reengage_after_days), and the system now records deliveries-per-question and latency-to-answer (first negative-signal channel). Planner queue items are marked sent when delivered. New config keys: adaptive_cadence, max_questions_per_day, reengage_after_days. Tests in tests/test_v68_loop.py.

v67: Entity identities stay stable across monthly roster refreshes, and the wiki cleans up after them. The AI roster resolution was stateless — build_prompt never saw the previous roster, so each month cold-started identity decisions and could re-split a merged person ('Grandma Betty Jo' with aliases became separate 'Grandma' and 'Betty Jo' entries, spawning duplicate pages and losing maps_to_focus mappings like Wife→Katie). Fixed three ways: (1) build_prompt now receives the previous roster for every entity type (direct-AI, --emit-task, and deterministic paths) and instructs the model to treat prior merges/mappings as settled — plus an explicit person rule that a kinship word (Grandma) and a proper name (Betty Jo) in overlapping answers are ONE entry; (2) a deterministic safety net (apply_previous_decisions) force-folds any output name/alias matching a previous entry back into that entry's canonical name before normalize, so slugs stay stable even if the model misbehaves; (3) wiki compile now removes orphaned origin:mention entity pages whose slug left the roster (never hand-authored/focus pages; skipped entirely when a type's roster is missing/empty), and source-lint gains two report-only rules — entity_page_not_in_roster and duplicate_entity_suspect (subset or ≥0.8-Jaccard source overlap between same-type pages). Tests added in tests/test_people_roster.py, tests/test_wiki_compile.py, tests/test_source_integrity.py.

v66: Initials-style names (AJ, JT) can now become people. Such names were invisible to the entire people pipeline at three independent choke points, so a brother mentioned ~40x as 'AJ' only ever surfaced as the generic label 'Brother'. Fixed: (1) recommend_focuses._extract_people name regex now accepts short all-caps initialisms (new _NAME_TOKEN = capitalized word OR [A-Z]{2,3}) and allows 2-char names (len>=2), with common acronyms (US, TV, CEO, …) added to STOPWORDS so the initialism branch doesn't mistake them for names; (2) entity_roster.load_candidates lowered its min-length gate from <3 to <2 so 2-char candidates reach the AI curator; (3) wiki_compile._mention_regex lowered its skip threshold from <3 to <2 (word boundaries still prevent substring hits) so scan_mentions finds the name and plan_entities can graduate the page. Single-char tokens are still excluded everywhere. Tests added in tests/test_v14_features.py, tests/test_people_roster.py, tests/test_wiki_compile.py. v65: Focus Recommendations no longer re-suggest people who are already a Focus under a different word. recommend() only excluded entities whose name matched an existing Focus subject (e.g. 'Dad'), so role words like 'Father', 'Mother', 'Wife' — which the AI-curated entity roster already maps to the Dad/Mom/Katie Focuses via maps_to_focus + aliases — were still surfaced as new-Focus candidates. New _focus_covered_aliases() reads the entity rosters and adds every name/alias of an entry with maps_to_focus set to the exclusion set, so those role words drop out. Test added in tests/test_v14_features.py. v64: Loop status page — fix the queue card and trim noise. The 'Queue delivered' card counted the queue items' own delivered flag, which nothing writes back, so it always read 0/N; it's now 'Queue answered' derived from the question bank (matching the Question Queue view). Also removes the 'Candidate pipeline' status-breakdown chips and the 'Detail views' link row (the hamburger menu already covers navigation), leaving just the at-a-glance card grid. Test updated in tests/test_wiki_views.py. v63: Wiki sidebar entity-type groups (People, Places, Projects, Themes, …) now start collapsed instead of open, so the sidebar opens as a scannable overview and you expand a group to see its pages. group_block renders each group with the 'collapsed' class by default; the localStorage persistence flipped from tracking collapsed groups to tracking expanded ones (key lifehug.expandedGroups), so any group you open stays open across navigation. Test added in tests/test_wiki_views.py. v62: Reorders the hamburger menu of dashboard views into logical groups (the VIEWS registry drives both the menu and the status-page links): The Loop, Graph, then the focus block (Focuses, Focus Recommendations), then the question surfaces (Question Bank, Question Candidates, Question Queue), then the rest (Coverage, Entity Candidates, Source Integrity). Test added in tests/test_wiki_views.py. v61: Question Bank view categories are now collapsible and start collapsed. Each category is a native <details>/<summary> element — the summary shows the category title and its progress bar (count + %), so the page opens as a scannable overview; clicking a row expands it to reveal that category's questions. No JavaScript (uses the browser's built-in disclosure widget with a rotating caret). Test added in tests/test_wiki_views.py. v60: Question Candidates view fills in the Quality and Category columns, which were always blank. Quality is not stored on candidates — it's computed on demand with check_quality (the same scorer the classifier and promotion gate use). Category is only stamped at review/promotion time, so for un-reviewed candidates the view now infers it via _infer_category (target_category → the candidate's neighborhood topic_type → bank letter), shown with the category name (e.g. 'E (Reflection & Wisdom)') and falling back to 'unassigned' only when nothing can be inferred. Tests added in tests/test_wiki_views.py. v59: Question Queue view shows weekly progress at a glance. Adds a progress bar at the top of the queue ('N of M answered · K remaining'), derived from the same bank-truth answered state as the per-row badges, so you can see how much of this week's plan is done without counting rows. Test added in tests/test_wiki_views.py. v58: Question Queue view shows answered state honestly. The status badge was derived only from the queue item's own delivered/queued flag — but nothing in the answer flow writes back to question_queue.json (ask.py reads the queue but never marks items), so a queued question you had already answered still read 'queued'. view_queue now derives status from the question bank (the source of truth for what's answered): each row shows answered (green), delivered (blue), or queued (yellow). Description updated; test added in tests/test_wiki_views.py. v57: Question Queue view is now human-readable. Queue items store only a question id and a bare category letter, so the dashboard's Question column was empty and the Cat column showed a cryptic letter. view_queue now resolves each row's question text and category name from the question bank (parse_questions/parse_categories): the Category column reads 'J (Vision)' instead of 'J', and the Question column shows the actual question text (falling back to the queue item's inline text if present). Column header renamed Cat → Category; test added in tests/test_wiki_views.py. v56: Fixes two long-standing updater bugs that silently corrupted framework files. (1) run_git returned stdout.strip(), so apply_version dropped the trailing newline from every file it wrote — leaving instances with dozens of one-byte diffs from upstream. File extraction now goes through read_repo_file_at (byte-exact bytes, written with write_bytes); run_git keeps stripping for token/list output. (2) The protection check used prefix matching for all PROTECTED_FILES entries, so the file entry 'config.yaml' also shadowed 'config.yaml.example' — meaning the example file could never be updated (instances were stuck on the pre-v35 version). New is_protected() matches file entries exactly and only treats trailing-slash entries as directory prefixes. Adds tests/test_update.py covering both fixes. v55: Dashboard view clarity pass (feedback from the hamburger-menu review). Every /views/<slug> page now carries a one-line description under its title explaining what the page is and what its data means (VIEW_DESCRIPTIONS, injected after the <h1> so empty states get it too). The Coverage view annotates each category letter with its title in parentheses (e.g. 'A (Origins)'). The Entity Candidates view now shows only entities still pending graduation — anything page-eligible or already mapped to a Focus has a wiki page and is dropped (the redundant Graduates column is gone), so the page no longer duplicates what the wiki already shows. The hamburger menu relabels 'Candidates' to 'Question Candidates' to distinguish it from Entity Candidates. Tests updated in tests/test_wiki_views.py. v54: Wiki gains a hamburger menu of read-only dashboard views. serve_wiki.py adds a three-line menu button right of the search bar whose dropdown is generated from a VIEWS registry (adding a view = one entry), and live /views/<slug> routes that render current state on each request: Focuses (the weekly progress/roadmap saturation bars as HTML, reusing roadmap.focus_fill + progress.verdict), Coverage (per-category status bars), Question Bank (categories with answered markers + coverage bars), Candidates (question_candidates grouped by status), Entity Candidates (entity rosters per type with graduation flags), Question Queue, Source Integrity (manifest + lint findings), Focus Recommendations, a Loop system-status dashboard, and an interactive entity Graph (self-contained vanilla-JS force layout via /views/graph.json: nodes sized by sources_count, filled by focus saturation or entity type, edges weighted by shared sources, click-through to pages). All views are Loop-adjacent and degrade gracefully on empty/missing state; existing pages, sidebar, and search are unchanged. Adds tests/test_wiki_views.py. v53: Adds autonomous-loop drift guardrails. Wrapper choices now reuse authoritative research/focus constants, research-expand exposes the keyless --from-response path, lower-level flags for classify verbosity, process-answer summaries, and entity roster force-empty are surfaced, monthly dry-run previews entity roster refreshes, monthly reports include research and roster output, and docs now distinguish monthly roster refresh from compile-time entity graduation. Regression tests lock the wrapper and scheduled-flow parity. v52: Surfaces learning-loop failures without blocking capture. Daily wiki compile, answer quality scoring, optional readiness refreshes, and weekly classification fallback now append inspectable records to state/learning_failures.jsonl; doctor reports recent learning-loop failures, weekly maintenance includes the same summary, and process-answer --commit stages state/ so answer_scores and related learning state are not omitted. v51: Protects symbolic object rosters from destructive refreshes. Object roster AI outages now preserve the existing roster instead of writing an empty fallback, successful object responses carry forward previously known symbolic objects unless explicitly replaced, and object-answer sampling spans the whole archive instead of only the first sorted answers. Adds regression tests for preservation and archive-wide sampling. v50: Makes the weekly planned queue honest by defaulting the delivery queue to 8 items across the planner, wrapper, and weekly maintenance script, matching the expiration horizon so tail items are not treated as committed daily prompts. README removes premature claims about automatic bank retirement and age-based float; candidate quality gating and planner quality multipliers remain documented. v49: Removes the completed person-roster migration bridge after Dave was migrated to state/entity_rosters/person.json. state/people_roster.json and system/people_roster.py are gone, entity-roster --type person is the only active roster path, and from-response accepts only the canonical entities schema. v48: Person rosters are canonical entity rosters. state/people_roster.json now migrates once into state/entity_rosters/person.json, active compiler paths read top-level entities only, Focus alias enrichment normalizes maps_to_focus against current Focus slugs, and people-roster is only a compatibility alias for entity-roster --type person. v47: Defines the Loop as Lifehug's canonical continuous-learning flow and adds Node/Edge graph terminology. README, AGENTS, CLAUDE, and README.template now distinguish In the Loop, Loop-adjacent, and Out of the Loop; they define Node/Node Type for graph reasoning while keeping Entity/Entity Type as the current product/code/frontmatter terms. Relationship pages represent Relationship Edges rather than generic node pages. v46: Relationship pages now use mention-enriched Focus evidence. plan_relationships keeps dedicated Focus answers primary, but can now graduate a Focus relationship page from enough cross-story mentions when no dedicated answers exist, preserving the dyadic relationship prompt lens and adding regression coverage for Dad-like cases. v45: Candidate operator surfaces now derive status choices from question_candidates.VALID_STATUSES, so list/review/update can inspect needs_review and auto_promoted without wrapper drift. Weekly dry-run now previews candidates-auto-promote before the real weekly job mutates the candidate store or question bank, with regression tests covering status parity and dry-run promotion coverage. v44: Neighborhood readiness now separates generated questions from captured answers. Output arcs track question_arc_completeness, promoted_completeness, answered_completeness, lifecycle counts, and ready_to_draft; progress only labels a neighborhood ready when answered material crosses the draft threshold, while promotion and answer flows refresh stored readiness. v43: Classifier joins the autonomous loop. classify_story now uses the same OpenClaw-first AI route as research expansion, dry-run previews without model calls or writes, classify-all accepts --limit, weekly_maintenance classifies a capped batch of unclassified sources before quality/profile/promotion, and classification files use repo-relative keys with legacy stem-only compatibility to avoid source-name collisions. README/CLAUDE/cron docs now show classification as the structured-understanding layer between immutable sources and reviewable candidates. v42: Wiki viewer renders italics. render_markdown/linkify only converted `**bold**` and `code`, so single-asterisk `*text*` and underscore `_text_` emphasis showed literal markers everywhere (answer labels like *Dave's answer:*, the index subtitle). Added `<em>` rules for both forms; the underscore form uses word-boundary guards so snake_case identifiers and file paths (source_manifest.json, entity_roster.py) aren't italicized. Render-only change; no wiki content is rewritten. v41: Periods read chronologically in the index. The period entity roster now carries an AI-assigned `chrono` rank (1 = earliest in life), set during roster curation (entity_roster build_prompt/normalize ask for and validate it); plan_entities passes it into period page frontmatter (new optional `chrono:` field), and update_index sorts the Periods section by that rank (earliest life stage on top — Childhood → My Teens → High School → College → My 20s …) instead of alphabetically. Pages without a rank sort last, alphabetical within ties; all other entity types stay alphabetical. v40: Stop the updater from clobbering the compiled index. `wiki/index.md` (the life-graph homepage, regenerated by `compile` from the author's answers — title = full_name, leading with the life-story block) and `wiki/log.md` (the author's compile activity log) were wrongly listed as framework_files, so every `update.py --apply` overwrote them with the shipped seed — reverting the index title from e.g. 'David James Taylor' back to 'Lifehug Wiki Index' and dropping the life-story section until the next compile regenerated it. Both are now removed from framework_files and added to PROTECTED_FILES, so updates never touch them (belt-and-suspenders: PROTECTED also guards against historical tags still listing them). wiki/SCHEMA.md stays framework-owned. Also fixes the index section list: update_index printed a header for EVERY entity type whether or not it had pages and pluralized them naively, producing empty/mangled '## Selfs' and '## Lifes_Works' sections — now empty types are skipped and headings use friendly labels (People/Self/Life's Work, mirroring serve_wiki's group labels). v39: Place/period graduation gated by AI + real mentions, not the noisy detector. The raw place detector undercounts real places (Mesa/San Diego show 1 hit though they appear across several answers), so place/period/object eligibility is now the AI's judgment (qualifies), and the 'a few mentions' bar is enforced at compile time against ACTUAL mention counts (plan_entities requires ≥2 real mentions for places/periods, ≥1 for people/objects). People keep their score/answers bar. v38: Entity graduation — the wiki builds out every node of the life graph, not just people. Fixes the bug where a bare `compile` (or process_answer/daily_question auto-compile) on a machine without an API key silently replaced synthesized pages with excerpt dumps. v25: README updated to reflect v24 autonomous quality loop.
